The application malfunctioned and would not allow the upload to be completed. 

Same-day follow-up on XX/XX/year> : Immediately after shipping the item, I contacted PayPal again and verbally provided the tracking number to a representative. I specifically asked three separate times whether any additional information from the shipping receipt was needed. I was told three separate times that nothing further was required, that the tracking information was sufficient, and that the case would be closed in my favor. 
Subsequent decision : Despite following PayPals instructions, providing the tracking number, returning the item, and paying return shipping costs myself, the case was once again decided against me and the funds were debited. 

XX/XX/year> : After continued effort, I was eventually able to upload the shipping receipt into the PayPal system. I have now been informed that the case has been appealed again and that it is expected to be resolved in my favor. However, I have received similar assurances multiple times throughout this process, only to have the outcome reversed without explanation.

PayPal Errors and Misrepresentations Throughout this dispute, I received conflicting and inconsistent information from PayPal representatives.

I was told that the seller would have five days to provide a return shipping label and that the case would be resolved in my favor if the seller failed to do so. The seller never provided a label, yet the case was closed the very next day.

After returning the item, I provided the tracking number directly to PayPal and repeatedly confirmed whether any additional documentation was required. d escalation to management at least six separate times. I repeatedly asked for a supervisor or member of upper management to contact me directly regarding the dispute. Those requests were denied, ignored, or never acted upon.

PayPals refusal to provide meaningful escalation prevented me from obtaining a fair review of the matter and left me with no effective way to address the contradictory information and decisions I was receiving.

Financial Impact As a direct result of PayPals actions and instructions, I have suffered financial losses and significant inconvenience.

I paid for an item that was not as represented and was later verified by a professional to be incorrect and defective. I then paid approximately {$40.00} in return shipping costs out of my own pocket based on PayPals instructions.

Despite complying with every instruction provided to me once I became aware of the alleged XX/XX/XXXX email, I have experienced repeated reversals, inconsistent guidance, and debiting of funds. I believe I was effectively deprived of both my money and the merchandise. 

In addition to the monetary losses, I have spent more than 10 hours attempting to resolve this matter through PayPals customer service channels.

Conclusion At this point, my complaint is not solely about the disputed transaction. It is also about PayPals dispute resolution process. I relied on instructions provided by PayPal representatives during recorded phone calls, incurred expenses based on those instructions, and complied with every request m
ade of me. Despite doing so, I experienced repeated reversals, inconsistent guidance, failure to escalate, and a lack of accountability.

Requested Remedies I respectfully request that the CFPB require PayPal to : 1. Conduct a complete review of all call recordings, representative notes, dispute communications, tracking information, a
nd uploaded documentation.

2. Reimburse the full disputed transaction amount.

3. Reimburse the approximately {$40.00} in return shipping expenses I incurred as a direct result of PayPals instructions.

4. Provide a written explanation of the contradictory decisions and representations made throughout the dispute process.

5. Review PayPals escalation procedures and refusal to provide management review when requested by consumers.

I have acted in good faith throughout this process and have complied with every instruction provided to me. The lack of consistency, accountability, and meaningful escalation has caused significant frustration, wasted time, and financial loss.

I am requesting that the CFPB reopen and review my complaint regarding Cash App 's handling of unauthorized Bitcoin purchases that were processed through my account.

On XX/XX/year>, multiple Bitcoin purchases were made through my Cash App account without my authorization. These transactions were entirely inconsistent with my account history, as I had no prior history of purchasing Bitcoin through Cash App.

My concern is no longer limited to the unauthorized transactions themselves. It now includes Cash App 's refusal to meaningfully investigate the matter, its reliance on unsupported conclusions, and its refusal to consider significant new evidence that directly contradicts its findings.

Cash App conducted an internal review and repeatedly concluded that the transactions were " authorized by you or someone you authorized to use your credentials '' and that " no error occurred. '' However, despite making this determination, Cash App has failed to provide any evidence supporting its conclusion.

In its responses, Cash App specifically stated that it reviewed my account history before reaching its decision. If my account history was in fact reviewed, then Cash App would have seen that I had never previously purchased Bitcoin. Rather than explaining how transactions that were completely inconsistent with my account 's historical activity were determined to be authorized, Cash App simply repeated its conclusion without providing supporting facts.

Throughout this process, I repeatedly asked Cash App to explain : What evidence was relied upon to determine the transactions were authorized.

What specific information from my account history supported that conclusion.

What fraud detection measures, alerts, or security reviews were triggered.

Why transactions that were inconsistent with my normal account activity were not flagged as suspicious.

How Cash App determined that no fraud or unauthorized access had occurred.

To date, none of these questions have been answered.

Instead, Cash App has continued to rely on unsupported conclusions while refusing to explain the basis for its findings. Simply stating that a transaction was authorized does not establish that it was authorized.

Additionally, Cash App repeatedly shifted focus to a related XXXX transaction even though my primary concern has always been the unauthorized Bitcoin purchases that occurred through Cash App itself. My complaint is centered on Cash App 's failure to detect, prevent, or adequately investigate fraudulent activity occurring on its own platform.

The most concerning issue is Cash App 's handling of new evidence that became available after its initial decision.

Cash App appears to be relying on the fact that the Bitcoin purchases were made from an XXXX that had previously been associated with my account. However, I informed Cash App, including Cash App manager XXXX, that this device had been legally sold to XXXX  and was no longer in my possession at the time the unauthorized transactions occurred. 

I have since filed a claim with XXXX  regarding that device and will be providing the XXXX  claim number and supporting documentation as part of this complaint. This evidence is directly relevant because it supports my position that the device used to access the account was no longer under my control. 

Despite being informed that the phone had been legally sold, despite being provided information regarding the XXXX  claim, and despite being notified that a formal law enforcement investigation is underway, Cash App refused to conduct any further review. Instead, XXXX informed me that Cash App had already thoroughly investigated the matter and closed the case without addressing any of the new information after requesting new information to be added and investigated.

The logic behind Cash App 's determination is deeply concerning. A device having once been associated with an account does not establish that future activity from that device is authorized. If a consumer legally sells a phone and the new possessor later accesses financial applications on that device and sends money to themselves or makes purchases, those transactions would not automatically become authorized simply because the device was once associated with the original owner.

Ownership and possession matter. The critical question is who had control of the device and account at the time of the transactions.

Rather than investigating whether unauthorized access occurred after the device left my possession, Cash App appears to have treated prior association with the device as proof of authorization. This conclusion ignores the evidence I provided and fails to address the possibility that the account was accessed by an unauthorized party.

This matter is now the subject of a formal law enforcement investigation. I have been informed that records from Cash App and XXXX will be requested as part of that investigation. Law enforcement has advised me that the transactions are being treated as unauthorized and efforts are underway to recover the stolen funds.

I am requesting a further review of Cash App 's investigation into over {$4500.00} in unauthorized XXXX transactions and a response regarding whether EcoATM was contacted to verify the ownership and possession status of the device relied upon in determining that those transactions were authorized. 

During Cash App 's investigation, I provided information to XXXX of the Cash App XXXX XXXX XXXX stating that the device identified as a " known device '' had been sold to XXXX months before the unauthorized transactions occurred. This information was directly relevant to Cash App 's conclusion because the device appears to have been a significant factor in determining that the transactions were authorized. 

After providing this information, I was never informed whether Cash App contacted XXXX to verify when the device came into its possession or whether the device was no longer in my possession at the time the unauthorized transactions occurred. The following day, my case was closed and the prior determination was maintained. 

I am requesting that Cash App provide information regarding whether XXXX was contacted as part of its investigation. If XXXX was contacted, I request that the results of that inquiry be provided. If XXXX was not contacted, I request an explanation as to how Cash App determined that activity originating from a device that had been sold months earlier supported a conclusion that the transactions were authorized by me. 

I am also attaching a police report and case number. The report documents that this matter was reported to law enforcement and supports my position that the transactions were unauthorized. If additional information or verification is needed, I encourage Cash App and/or the CFPB to contact the law enforcement agency listed in the report directly. I have been fully transparent throughout this process and welcome any efforts to independently verify the facts surrounding this case.

I am concerned that the information I provided was not fully considered. XXXX advised me that if I had new supporting information, I should provide it for consideration. In response, I immediately provided information obtained through my own investigation showing that the device relied upon as a " known device '' had been sold to XXXX  months before the unauthorized XXXX transactions occurred. 

This information was important because it directly challenged the conclusion that the transactions were authorized simply because they originated from a device previously associated with my account. A device that is no longer in someone's possession can still be used by another person, and activity originating from that device should not automatically be considered authorized by the former owner. 

After I provided this information, my case was closed the following day and the prior conclusion was maintained. Based on the timing, I have serious concerns about whether this new information was meaningfully investigated before a final determination was made. 

To date, I have not been provided with evidence showing that I personally initiated, approved, or authorized the disputed XXXX purchases. Instead, the determination appears to rely heavily on the fact that the activity originated from a device that had once been associated with my account, despite evidence that the device had been sold and was no longer in my possession. 

This situation is no different than if someone took someones phone and transferred money from that Cash App account attached to that phone without permission. The fact that a transaction is completed from a device or account associated with the account holder does not automatically mean the account holder authorized it. Authorization requires the account holder 's knowledge and consent. If another individual accessed my account and conducted these transactions without my permission, then those transactions were not authorized, regardless of what device or account information was used to complete them. 

Cash App has also continued to maintain that XXXX bears responsibility because the funds originated from my XXXX account. However, regardless of where the funds originated, the disputed XXXX purchases occurred within Cash App 's platform and were processed through my Cash App account and then gone. 

The transactions involved multiple XXXX purchases occurring within a very short period of time on an account with no history of XXXX activity. Given the nature, speed, and volume of these transactions, I believe they should have triggered additional fraud reviews or security measures. At a minimum, these circumstances appear unusual enough to warrant closer scrutiny before allowing the transactions to proceed. 

Cash App publicly represents to consumers that it protects users from fraud and utilizes fraud monitoring and proactive security features designed to help prevent fraud before it occurs. In my case, those protections appear to have failed. Multiple unauthorized XXXX purchases were completed despite several apparent indicators of potential fraud. 

Because of that, I believe it is reasonable to ask what fraud detection measures, if any, were triggered and why the activity was allowed to proceed despite the unusual nature of the transactions. 

For these reasons, I do not believe responsibility should be shifted entirely to XXXX. While I am also pursuing accountability from XXXX regarding allowing my phone number to be removed and all money quickly transferred, Cash App was the platform that processed the disputed XXXX transactions and had the opportunity to identify potential fraud indicators before those transactions were completed. 

Cash App has also indicated that the transactions were verified using my debit card information. However, I do not believe this establishes that I personally authorized the transactions. If an unauthorized individual gained access to my Cash App account via the broken XXXX sold to EcoATM, they would have had access to information displayed within the Cash App account, including my whole debit card number on the account. In that circumstance, the ability to provide or verify debit card information would not necessarily prove that the transactions were authorized by me. Rather, it could be consistent with an individual who had already gained unauthorized access to my account via the sold XXXX to XXXXand the information available within it. 

I am asking for a thorough review of all available evidence, including the attached police report, the information regarding the previously sold device, and any available account access records that may assist in determining the true source of the unauthorized activity.

This situation has had a significant impact on my family. That money taken was not just numbers on a screen ; it was money that my family depends on. Since discovering the unauthorized activity, I have spent countless hours trying to understand what happened, report it to the appropriate parties, and recover the funds that were taken.

I am trying to understand how this happened and recover funds that I did not authorize to be spent. 

I remain fully committed to pursuing this matter until the unauthorized funds are reimbursed and this situation is properly resolved. I am filing a formal dispute against USAA for a clear violation of Regulation E ( Electronic Fund Transfer Act ) error-resolution requirements following an unauthorized Electronic Fund Transfer ( EFT ) of {$19000.00}. 

On XX/XX/year>, fraudsters impersonating the USAA Fraud Department called me. They asked if I had made a {$1000.00} purchase at XXXX and {$500.00} at XXXX. I responded " No '' to both. Then they said there was an additional flag showing that someone had tried to repeatedly make a wire transfer from my account, in-person from a local XXXX bank. They asked if I had my drivers license and debit card in my possession since the only way someone could do the transaction was to physically have those documents. I told them I had them and that I had never been to that bank branch. 

The fraudster proceeded to tell me that they were going to investigate the account. They sent me a verification text code to 'verify my identity and the account info ' and asked me to read it back to them. They used this code to execute an Account Takeover ( ATO ). Once inside my portal, they quickly altered my account 's custom nicknames to read " Under Investigation '' and changed the viewing preferences so that I could not see my balances at a glance instead, my bank apps Home Screen said " Balances Hidden. '' I later learned that during this time, they also transferred {$20000.00} from my savings account to my checking account and authorized an increase in my daily debit card transaction limit to {$20000.00}. 

Then the fraudster said that someone at the XXXX bank branch was trying to initiate the wire transfers and that I needed to immediately to go the bank to do a 'test ' transaction and see if the transaction was faulty or if someone at the bank was doing something nefarious. 

The fraudster kept me on the phone the whole time I drove to the bank, making everything seem urgent and harried. They told me when I got inside the bank to look for anything that seemed suspicious like agents not wearing name badges, on their phone, being nervous, etc. They told me to fill out a deposit slip in the amount {$19000.00}, account number XXXX, and name : " XXXX LLC ''. They said to take it to the teller and ask for a cash transfer from my USAA account to the account on the slip and to get 'both receipts '. I had asked repeatedly if I was going to see any deduction from my account and they assured me I wouldn't. 

I did the transaction and left the bank. They asked me questions like " was anyone acting suspicious, was everyone wearing their name badge. '' They said to go home and they would show me where on the USAA website to upload the receipts to submit for the fraud claim. 

When I got home, they said that it appeared that shortly after my transaction at the bank someone tried to initiate a wire with my husband 's information at the same bank. I had been on the phone over an hour and a half. At this point, my husband was listening in on the conversation and we started asking questions. They abruptly hung up the phone. 

I immediately called USAA and relayed all this to the claims/fraud department. That is when they informed me that someone had gone into my account and raised our debit card limit and transferred money from my savings to my checking account. 

After filing the claim with USAA, we went back to XXXX bank branch and got a copy of the deposit slip. They said that it was a cash advance, not a wire transfer that was initiated. They said that the money was deposited into a XXXX bank account but that they could not put a hold on the funds being released until they received notification from USAA. XXXX suggested we file a police report, which we did with XXXX XXXX XXXX in Pennsylvania ( in the jurisdiction where the bank operates and we live ). 

USAA has denied my initial fraud claim and an appeal, arguing that because I provided the 2FA passcode and physically used my card, the transaction was " authorized. '' This is a direct violation of official CFPB Regulation E Guidance ( Electronic Fund Transfers FAQs : Section 2 on Unauthorized EFTs ). The CFPB explicitly states that when a consumer is fraudulently induced into providing validation credentials or passcodes to an entity misrepresenting itself as the financial institution, the resulting transfer is legally Unauthorized. The root cause of this loss was a successful account takeover facilitated by deceptive credential harvesting. 

The CFPB explicitly states that if a criminal tricks you into giving up account credentials ( like a password or a 2FA code ) by pretending to be your bank, you did not grant permission to be robbed. And Federal consumer protection regulations always override any private bank policies that might state, " If you share your password or 2FA code, you are responsible for all losses. '' I am requesting that CFPB demand that USAA honor federal law, reverse their denial, and credit my account for the {$19000.00}.

Relying on those representations and acting in good faith, I sent {$1900.00} through XXXX to XXXX XXXX, using the XXXX account registered under XXXX. 

Shortly after the transfer, I discovered that my friend 's XXXX account had been hacked and was being used by an unknown individual to impersonate him and solicit money from his contacts. I immediately realized that I had been deceived by a criminal actor who exploited a trusted relationship and a compromised communication platform. 

Following discovery of the fraud, I immediately notified Bank of America and submitted a fraud claim. I provided all information available to me regarding the impersonation scheme and the circumstances surrounding the transaction. Despite my prompt reporting and cooperation, Bank of America denied my claim and refused reimbursement. 

After receiving the bank 's denial, I reported the matter to the XXXX XXXX Police Department. The incident was documented under Police Report XXXX. XXXX, and the police investigation identified the crime as Theft by Deception. The report confirms that the perpetrator used my friend 's compromised XXXX account to impersonate him and fraudulently obtain money from individuals who reasonably believed they were communicating with a trusted contact. 

The bank 's position appears to be based solely on the fact that I physically initiated the transfer. However, that conclusion ignores the critical fact that my authorization was procured through fraud and criminal impersonation. 

I did not knowingly send money to a scammer, a stranger, or an unauthorized recipient. Rather, I intended to send money to a person whom I personally knew and trusted. The transaction occurred only because a third-party criminal successfully impersonated that individual through a hacked communications account. 

This distinction is significant. Consumers are routinely advised by XXXX and participating financial institutions to send money only to people they know and trust. In this case, I followed that guidance. I was attempting to assist someone I knew personally. The fraud occurred because a criminal actor compromised a trusted communication channel and exploited that relationship. 

The circumstances of this case demonstrate a growing consumer protection issue involving person-to-person payment platforms. Fraudsters increasingly gain access to legitimate communication accounts and impersonate trusted individuals, making it difficult for consumers to detect the deception. Under these circumstances, consumers may reasonably believe they are acting consistently with the warnings and guidance provided by payment platforms. 

Additionally, after my experience became known within my community, other individuals reported receiving similar fraudulent requests from the same compromised account. As a result of this incident, I suffered a financial loss of {$1900.00}, which has not been recovered. Despite reporting the fraud promptly and providing supporting documentation, Bank of America has completely denied my claim and I have received no reimbursement. 

I respectfully request that Bank of America reopen and reconsider its decision and that the CFPB assist in facilitating a fair review of this matter.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am submitting a complaint regarding JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.s handling of a XXXX claim for approximately {$1200.00} tied to a XX/XX/year> payment to XXXX. 

This complaint is not limited to reimbursement. It is also about Chases contradictory, misleading, and perfunctory handling of the matter from intake through closure. I contacted Chase to dispute a XXXX payment that I authorized only because I was induced to do so through deceptive representations surrounding a purported sublease arrangement, a purported contract, and related assurances that made the transaction appear legitimate and protected when it was not. I explained to Chase that the arrangement was presented as official, that a written contract was used to make it appear formal, that my drivers license was photographed for processing, and that I later determined the contract was not legitimate in the way it was represented and that the stated terms and conditions were not honored.

During the calls, Chase representatives gave inconsistent and confusing explanations about whether the matter could even be processed. One representative stated that the matter would be transferred to claims to report this, get investigated, and also get the funds back, and also stated that the transaction and reason for dispute had already been placed on file. A later representative then told me that the dispute was not going through, that Chase was unable to reverse it because it was an authorized self-payment, that there was no debit card involved, that XXXX was a third party, that Chase had no recovery rights for XXXX payments , and that Regulation E did not apply because my card was not involved. Despite those statements, the same representative also stated, Ive gone ahead and filed a claim. The claim then appeared in the Chase portal, was shown as opened, and was closed the same day.

That sequence is exactly why I am complaining. Chases handling appears contradictory, perfunctory, and misleading. If Chases position is that it will not honor this type of claim, then it should say so clearly, consistently, and based on an identifiable written policy. Instead, I received a series of shifting explanations that suggested the representatives themselves were either improvising, misapplying policy, or attempting to discourage or narrow the complaint before it could be fully reviewed. The fact that the claim was both said to be non-viable and nevertheless filed, then closed the same day, raises serious concerns about whether Chase performed any meaningful review at all.

I am also concerned about misleading signals created by Chases own payment flow and prior oral statements. Chases XXXX interface asked me to identify the nature or purpose of the payment, including a service-related classification, which reasonably suggested that the nature of the transaction could matter for risk review, complaint handling, or dispute processing. I was also previously told by a Chase employee that there was a much longer period in which claims could be raised. Later, however, Chase representatives told me that authorized XXXX disputes involving service issues, non-performance, or similar problems effectively would not be processed. If Chase collects purpose-of-payment information but later treats that classification as meaningless when a consumer seeks help, that is misleading. If Chase representatives are telling consumers materially different things about what is reviewable, what deadlines exist, and whether any complaint path exists at all, that is also misleading.

I want Chase to provide a clear written explanation of the following : what the purpose-of-payment classification in the XXXX flow actually means ; whether Chase has a formal complaint, escalation, or review process for authorized XXXX payments involving deception , fake or misleading contract representations, non-performance, or service-related disputes ; the exact written policy basis for the statements I received that the claim could not go through ; why I was told the matter would be investigated and put on file, only for Chase to later say it was not viable while still filing the claim ; why the claim was opened and closed the same day ; whether any evidence review occurred before closure ; whether the recorded calls will be preserved and reviewed ; and whether the representatives involved were following written policy or giving incorrect and improvised explanations.

To be clear, I did not present this to Chase as a routine buyers remorse issue. I reported it as a scam or deceptive-inducement situation involving a purported sublease, a purported contract used to create a false sense of legitimacy, and representations that caused me to authorize the payment under false pretenses. Chases handling of that report was inconsistent from start to finish and did not provide a clear, fair, or transparent complaint process.

The portal also stated that Chase had sent a letter detailing the outcome, but no outcome letter or attached decision document was available to me in the claim or notices area at the time I checked.

I am asking CFPB to require Chase to review this matter properly, preserve and review the recorded calls, provide a written explanation addressing the contradictions described above, and explain whether Chases current intake and handling of these XXXX complaints is misleading to consumers.
